summary:
MARGA (Mars Adaptive Route Guidance Architecture) is a decision-support prototype that helps future Mars explorers find scientifically interesting sites and plan routes to them.
The problem it tackles is simple: the most interesting site is not always the safest or easiest one to reach. Planning a traverse means combining science observations, imagery, elevation, terrain, routes and mission time, which an ordinary map does not do.
In MARGA, the user picks a science objective, sees relevant NASA observations on an interactive Mars map, chooses a target and gets a terrain-aware route with its distance, travel time and a first check on whether there is enough time to return.
Objectives are linked to data through a fixed, rule-based catalogue (no machine learning). A Python geospatial engine plans routes with A*, and a React and TypeScript frontend shows the results on the map.
The first prototype covers Gale Crater and Mount Sharp, where Curiosity and the orbiters have collected a lot of data. We use verified datasets where possible and clearly mark missing, uncertain or low-resolution data.

details:
Github : https://github.com/Cryogenicboom/MARGA

MARGA (Mars Adaptive Route Guidance Architecture) is an offline-first, lightweight Mars surface exploration and route-planning application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the "Create a Martian Map" challenge. Focused on Gale Crater and Mount Sharp, MARGA integrates NASA planetary datasets, including HiRISE-derived elevation models, CTX imagery, and scientific observations from the Curiosity rover, such as CheMin mineralogical records and Navcam panoramas, into an interactive geospatial decision-support workstation.

At its core, MARGA uses a terrain-aware pathfinding engine based on the A* algorithm to calculate traversable routes by considering elevation, slope, surface roughness and configurable terrain constraints. Users can compare routes optimized for lowest terrain cost, shortest distance or fastest estimated travel time, examine elevation profiles, explore scientific targets and assess return journeys against configured EVA (Extravehicular Activity) time budgets and safety reserves.

By combining planetary mapping, scientific observations, terrain analysis and mission planning in one application, MARGA aims to make fragmented planetary data more accessible and actionable for future human exploration of Mars.

The project was developed using React, TypeScript, Python, OpenLayers, GeoPandas, Shapely with Web Workers enabling background route computation. Its creative contribution lies in connecting scientific target selection with terrain-aware navigation and independent return-route assessment rather than merely displaying a map or calculating the geometrically shortest path.

MARGA is currently an experimental research and decision-support prototype; its terrain data is not validated for operational navigation, its mobility calculations use simplified assumptions, and its radiation estimates are based on historical Curiosity RAD measurements rather than real-time monitoring.
